paths.description: Public marketing homepage, including global navigation, hero carousel, consent UI, dark/reduced-motion/high-contrast conditions, and mobile reflow.
Pricing archetype and primary commercial decision surface; used for performance, network, accessibility, metadata, and memory evidence.
Creator signup entry and account form, including labels, autocomplete, pricing/terms disclosure, and identity-provider choices.
Login route reconnaissance. Cloudflare verification appeared in the independent login capture, so login-specific observations were not used to claim flow completion.

findings.summary: The public marketing surface does not declare or adapt a document color scheme.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the computed probe reports colorScheme "normal" and transparent body background rather than a dark-aware document palette.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and express non-photographic surfaces, dialogs, text, and controls with preference-aware color tokens or light-dark().

findings.summary: The consent dialog is not robust under increased contrast.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast: more screenshot shows the middle consent action as a blue button with no visible label, while its label is visible in the ordinary desktop capture.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system-aware foreground/background tokens for all consent actions, test forced colors, and preserve text with forced-color-adjust only where strictly necessary.

findings.summary: The marketing bundle relies on main-thread animation libraries instead of a declarative motion baseline.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse code coverage identifies GSAP, ScrollTrigger, and Lenis in the shared app bundle; no active ScrollTimeline was observed in the rendered probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Move scroll-linked effects to CSS scroll-driven animations, use native scrolling rather than Lenis where possible, and use View Transitions for state or route changes with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: The cookie dialog dominates the first mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the consent surface occupies most of the lower viewport and obscures the hero copy and primary page content on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent surface while retaining equally prominent accept and reject actions and a clear path to detailed choices.

findings.summary: The throttled mobile load misses the LCP performance bar by a wide margin.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports performance 56, FCP 3.3 s, LCP 13.1 s, Speed Index 15.3 s, and time to interactive 55.5 s; CLS remains good at 0.00032.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP image, stop lazy-loading above-the-fold hero media, reduce font and script competition, and shorten critical request chains.

findings.summary: The pricing page transfers an extraordinary font payload.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary records 25,087,774 transferred bytes, of which 21,890,918 bytes are six fonts; four Noto CJK variable fonts alone account for about 21.4 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset fonts by locale and script, load only the active locale, apply font-display, and avoid shipping SC, TC, JP, and KR font families to every visitor.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and expensive shared animation code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 534 KiB of unused JavaScript, including 88.7% of app.js, and reports 4.0 s main-thread work with 1.44 s in script evaluation.
findings.suggestedFix: Split marketing routes by template, remove unused parsers and animation libraries from the pricing entry, and defer analytics and consent implementation code until needed.

findings.summary: Pricing details and supporting copy fail minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse axe-core reports ratios as low as 1.83:1 for fee details and 2.99:1 for multiple card descriptions against white, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken secondary text tokens and verify every pricing-card state at 4.5:1 for normal text, including links and disabled-looking copy that remains essential.

findings.summary: The pricing page contains an invalid heading-level jump.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies the H4 "Your world to create" as an invalid heading-order transition; the page also exposes two separate H1 headings.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page-level H1 and derive all section heading levels from document structure rather than visual size.

findings.summary: The page emits a Cloudflare RUM CORS error during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records a blocked XMLHttpRequest to cloudflareinsights.com/cdn-cgi/rum and a corresponding net::ERR_FAILED console error.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the RUM endpoint CORS setup or suppress the request when it cannot succeed so production pages load without console errors.

findings.summary: Production JavaScript has missing or incomplete source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports app.js without a source map and several Next.js chunk maps with missing sourcesContent entries.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid protected production source maps to the error-monitoring pipeline and ensure chunk maps contain resolvable sources.

findings.summary: Important browser-enforced security policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The header probe finds no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options or observed frame-ancestors policy, no Permissions-Policy, and HSTS max-age of only 30 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce- or hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors, extend HSTS after rollout validation, and add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Two first-party cookies lack Secure and all observed cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.evidence: The cookie probe reports analytics_session_id and patreon_currency_pref without Secure; patreon_device_id is retained for 400 days; all five observed cookies have SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, use Lax or Strict unless cross-site delivery is required, shorten device identifiers, and document each SameSite=None exception.

findings.summary: The public page has a broad third-party and analytics footprint.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 27 third-party requests and 2.35 MB from third-party origins; the tracker probe observes Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics, Sentry, and ten third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential tags until consent, remove duplicate telemetry, self-host essential assets where justified, and batch minimal analytics events.

findings.summary: The visible creator signup offers federated identity and passwords but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The signup DOM exposes Google, Apple, Facebook, email, and current-password controls; no WebAuthn or passkey action is present in the audited entry state.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey creation and authentication as a first-class option, retaining federated sign-in and password recovery as compatible fallbacks.

findings.summary: Public marketing pages omit canonical URLs.
findings.evidence: Both rendered probes and the 200 raw pricing HTML contain no rel=canonical, although 20 hreflang links, search-allowing robots rules, and a sitemap are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a self-referencing canonical for every indexable marketing template and keep canonical, hreflang, sitemap, and redirect targets consistent.

findings.summary: The pricing and organization surfaces have social metadata but no structured data.
findings.evidence: The rendered and raw probes find seven Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks on the pricing template.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization and service or offer structured data that matches the visible pricing content, and validate it with a structured-data tester.

findings.summary: Hero and decorative images waste more than a megabyte on mobile.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,354 KiB savings: the PNG hero wastes about 749 KiB and a 95x95 animated logo transfers about 639 KiB.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF or WebP hero variants sized to the rendered breakpoint, compress the animated logo aggressively, and avoid lazy-loading the above-the-fold LCP image.
